items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Eddie had studied with him years ago so this man Scholnick got Charles Elgar to organize a band for Eddie... We rehearsed for a few weeks to get the band into shape

ctx.x: He thought he could do it.

At that time Eddie had a piano player named Spaulding out of Kentucky, fantastic player, classical… more to the type player, not much jazz. Cliff King, a clarinet player called Clarinet King, marvelous player. He was doing that thing where you break the clarinet down and wind up playing just the mouthpiece. He could do all that kind of stuff. Stanley Wilson, a guitar player was playing a four-string guitar. He had a drummer from South America some place in this band. So this guy was thinking about bringing him…
Cigar rollers, right [laugh], after the talking pictures.
